title: Folder runs apply the first preset's timeout to every preset in the folder
existing_state: ExecuteFolderWithOptionsAsync computes one timeout for the whole folder: `int commandTimeout = presets.Values.FirstOrDefault()?.Timeout ?? config.Timeout;` (Form1.cs:12916) and passes a single SshTimeoutOptions into `_sshService.ExecuteFolderAsync` (12917-12929). SshExecutionService never re-resolves per-preset timeouts — the only timeout reads in the service are `timeouts.CommandTimeout` (SshExecutionService.cs:1628, 2226) and `timeouts.ConnectionTimeout` (2375). Per CLAUDE.md, `int? Timeout` is the one per-preset override that exists, and it is honored for single-preset runs (Form1.cs:12307-12309) — but in a folder run, every preset after the first runs under the first preset's (or default) timeout.
recommendation: Thread per-preset timeouts into the folder pipeline: either pass `Dictionary<string, SshTimeoutOptions>` (or resolve `preset.Timeout ?? defaultTimeout` inside ExecuteFolderAsync's per-preset loop in SshExecutionService) so each preset executes with its own configured timeout. Keep ConnectionTimeout shared.
user_benefit: A long-running preset (firmware upgrade, large transfer) placed after a quick preset in a folder is currently killed at the quick preset's timeout — runs fail with timeout errors that look like host problems, and the per-preset Timeout setting the user configured is silently ignored.

evidence.note: Single timeout from first preset for entire folder run
ExecuteFolderAsync takes one SshTimeoutOptions; no per-preset timeout resolution anywhere in the service (only timeouts.CommandTimeout at 1628/2226)
